$comment: PLAT-838 M2 labelled corpus. AGENT-LABELLED, NOT HUMAN GROUND TRUTH: every `labels` block below was assigned by the agent authoring this evaluation harness, reading each statement the same way the skill's step 2 asks a human to. No second human reader adjudicated these. `engine_naive_pattern` is this agent's mechanical application of FR-042's documented EARS keyword rule (When->event_driven, While->state_driven, If...then->unwanted_behaviour, Where->optional_feature, no trigger->ubiquitous, a non-canonical trigger word canonicalised to the pattern it would imply once reworded) -- these are synthetic statements written for this corpus, not real spec files, so `quire validate` was not run against them; `engine_naive_pattern_method` states this per row. Fixtures 002 and 003/016 satisfy PLAT-838's acceptance criteria: a When that is really a While (002, 007-as-If), and a statement passing the vague-verb denylist but unmeasurable (003).

fixtures.statement_text: When the user submits the login form, the system SHALL authenticate the credentials within 2 seconds.

labels.note: Sound event pattern, concrete threshold (2 seconds).

fixtures.statement_text: When the system is under heavy load, the system SHALL degrade gracefully by disabling non-critical background jobs.

labels.note: PLAT-838 acceptance case: 'is under heavy load' names a sustained condition, not a momentary event -- this is really a While. Engine parses it as a grammatically clean When statement and has no way to see this.

fixtures.statement_text: The system SHALL be robust to malformed input files.

labels.note: PLAT-838 acceptance case: 'robust' is not in the vague-response denylist (support/handle/manage/process/provide/enable/be able to), so the engine's denylist check does not fire, yet the response names no observable, falsifiable behaviour.

fixtures.statement_text: The system SHALL persist every configuration change to disk before acknowledging the write request.

labels.note: Sound ubiquitous requirement with an observable, falsifiable outcome.

fixtures.statement_text: While the export job is running, the system SHALL reject new export requests with a 409 status.

labels.note: Sound state pattern; the sustained condition and the measurable response both match the While reading.

fixtures.statement_text: If the checksum verification fails, then the system SHALL abort the write and roll back the partial file.

labels.note: Sound unwanted-behaviour pattern: the condition is genuinely undesired and phrased canonically.

fixtures.statement_text: When the disk quota is exceeded, the system SHALL refuse further writes and emit a QUOTA_EXCEEDED error.

labels.note: The third judgment step 2 names: 'the disk quota is exceeded' is an undesired condition stated with When instead of If...then. Engine parses it as a clean event statement.

fixtures.statement_text: Where telemetry is enabled, the system SHALL emit a heartbeat event every 30 seconds.

labels.note: Sound optional-feature pattern with a concrete interval.

fixtures.statement_text: While the cluster is in maintenance mode, when a new deployment is requested, the system SHALL queue the request until maintenance ends.
fixtures.engine_naive_pattern_method: mechanical: state trigger + event trigger combined -> complex

labels.note: A genuine compound pattern (sustained state gating a discrete event); complex is the right EARS reading, not a defect.

fixtures.statement_text: Upon completion of the nightly backup, the system SHALL send a summary email to the operations distribution list.
fixtures.engine_naive_pattern_method: mechanical: 'Upon' canonicalises to 'When' -> event_driven (the engine itself flags this row's wording as ears:non-canonical-trigger; this fixture asks whether Jev's semantic reading is nonetheless correct)

labels.note: The engine's non-canonical-trigger finding is a wording defect it already catches; the underlying pattern this lens judges is genuinely event-driven, so this is a no-defect row for the SEMANTIC layer even though the engine's own grammar pass is not clean on this line.

fixtures.statement_text: When the queue backs up, the system SHALL shed the lowest-priority 10% of pending jobs.

labels.note: Genuinely ambiguous: 'backs up' can read as a threshold-crossing instant (sound When) or an ongoing backlog condition (really a While). Recorded both ways rather than resolved, per this ticket's own instruction to include cases the lens is expected to find hard.

fixtures.statement_text: The system SHALL be available during business hours.

labels.note: 'Available' with no stated threshold or SLA is unmeasurable on the strict reading; a lenient reading treats it as a binary health-check pass. Recorded both ways.

fixtures.statement_text: When the API receives a webhook payload with an invalid signature, the system SHALL respond with HTTP 401 and log the request id.

labels.note: Sound event pattern, concrete measurable response (a specific status code and a logging side effect).

fixtures.statement_text: Parsing SHALL complete in under 200 milliseconds for documents up to 10,000 lines.

labels.note: Per-archetype dialect: an NFR with no trigger is fine (SKILL.md's own Notes section) -- this is a control row confirming Jev does not manufacture a trigger-based finding where the engine's own dialect rule says there is none to find.

fixtures.statement_text: The platform operator SHALL have a single dashboard showing the health of every registered service.

labels.note: Per-archetype dialect: StR may use a stakeholder subject (SKILL.md's own Notes section) -- a control row confirming Jev does not flag the stakeholder-subject phrasing itself as a defect.

fixtures.statement_text: The system SHALL provide meaningful error messages to the user.

labels.note: Control row: the engine's own vague-response denylist already catches 'provide', so this is not a delta case -- included to confirm Jev's independent unmeasurability judgment agrees with the engine on an easy one, not to claim credit for a defect the engine already finds.
